text_blocks.snippet: Recurrent Lyme disease can refer to either reinfection with Lyme disease or post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS), where symptoms persist after antibiotic treatment. Reinfection involves a new infection with the bacteria Borrelia burgdorferi, while PTLDS refers to persistent symptoms like fatigue, pain, and cognitive problems following treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: reinfection with Lyme disease or post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS), where symptoms persist after antibiotic treatment

list.snippet: It's possible to get Lyme disease more than once, as the body doesn't develop long-term immunity to the bacteria.
Multiple episodes of Lyme disease, including recurring erythema migrans (the characteristic rash), can be caused by reinfection from different strains of the bacteria.
